subject: Data custody SLAs and temporary-hop authorization for CardioHealth
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@cardiohealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@cardiohealth.com
Date: 2027-09-28T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Data custody SLAs and temporary-hop authorization for CardioHealth

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and security teams have one set of operational questions we need answered before we can sign the DPA: specifically around temporary cross-region processing (backup/ingestion windows), KMS key custody when a transient hop occurs, and the subprocessors you route to in APAC for analytics.

I've attached a redline of the DPA (CardioHealth_DPA_redline_20270928.pdf) and the subprocessor roster we received earlier — please confirm the following points or propose contract language we can accept: 

- Can Redwood accept a 72-hour maximum transient hop (temporary cross-region processing) with explicit notification and audit evidence?
- For transient hops, does Redwood hold ciphertext only and will keys remain under our control (bring-your-own-key) or is there a split-KMS model?
- We need confirmation that analytics/monitoring telemetry routed to APAC is pseudonymized and that PII is not exported.
- A single consolidated attachment with the finalized subprocessor roster and expected activation windows would help our procurement team.

Please loop in ops or security as needed. If there's a standard operational runbook or evidence packet you can share (audit logs, TTL for caches, region pinning enforcement examples), that would speed review on our side.

Best,
Emma
Emma Liu | Sr. Security PM, CardioHealth

Attachments: CardioHealth_DPA_redline_20270928.pdf; subprocessor_roster_2027-09.csv

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@cardiohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-28T11:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data custody SLAs and temporary-hop authorization for CardioHealth

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. We can commit to operational guardrails that match what you're asking; a few specifics below and an ask for one small concession in the DPA redline (see attached operational draft).

1) 72-hour transient hop: We can accept a documented 72-hour temporary cross-region processing window for failover/ingestion/backups with the following controls:
   - Pre-authorized activation by CardioHealth (API token + signed request) or an emergency ops trigger that we notify immediately;
   - Full audit trail retained for 13 months showing invocation, changed routing, and affected request ids;
   - Automatic revert to pinned region once capacity stabilizes.

2) KMS and key custody: We offer BYOK (customer-provided keys) for primary data-at-rest. For transient hops, keys remain under your control; Redwood will support a split-KMS workflow for any short-term assist operations (we do not retain plaintext). Operationally we will:
   - Accept encrypted payloads with client-side wrapping and only unwrap under a supervised operation window (72h max);
   - Provide HSM attestations and a key-use log per operation.

3) Analytics telemetry: We will pseudonymize any telemetry routed to APAC and ensure PII fields are stripped before export. We'll share a sample telemetry schema and the transform rules.

4) Subprocessor roster and activation windows: Please confirm the attached CSV matches your copy; we'll provide an activation calendar that maps each subprocessor to an expected activation window and data categories processed.

I've attached an operational-custody-sla-draft.docx that frames the clauses we implement operationally (routing triggers, audit proofs, KMS flow). Marissa and Karthik are cc'd to add SLA thresholds (latency/retention) and legal wording.

If that aligns, we can put the operational runbook into a DPA annex and send a DocuSign packet for sign-off.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachments: operational-custody-sla-draft.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@cardiohealth.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-29T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data custody SLAs and temporary-hop authorization for CardioHealth

Emma — a few operational clarifications from our side to make sure the annex matches CardioHealth's risk appetite: 

- Audit evidence: We'll provide a per-request routing log (request id, timestamp, source region, destination region, operator id) and a summarized activation report after any transient hop event. Delivery via secure share (S3 presigned or secure Drive) within 48 hours of request.

- Retention and telemetry: Routing logs + key-use logs will be retained 13 months by default; we can extend retention under enterprise support if you require it. Telemetry exported to APAC will be limited to non-PII metrics and hashed identifiers; the transform rules will be included in the annex.

- SLA: For pinned-region requests our P95 latency SLO remains unchanged. For transient-hop activations we define an "activation acknowledgement" SLA of 1 hour and an "activation completion" target of 6 hours for the routing change to be in effect (documented in the runbook).

- Escrow/Breakglass: For extreme incidents we support a temporary escrow mode where an on-call engineer accepts a cardholder-signed breakglass token; these events are fully logged and require a post-event review.

Karthik — can you confirm the KMS attestation format we plan to share (FIPS/HSM cert reference + signed log) so Emma has the exact artifact type?

Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@cardiohealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@cardiohealth.com
Date: 2027-10-01T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data custody SLAs and temporary-hop authorization for CardioHealth

Thanks — this level of detail is very helpful. CardioHealth legal is comfortable with the proposed 72-hour window provided we get: 

- The annex language locking the 72-hour cap and requiring notification within 1 hour of activation;
- Delivery of the routing log within 48 hours after an activation; and
- The KMS attestation artifact (FIPS-compliant HSM certificate + signed key-use log) included as schedule B.

We'll accept the BYOK / split-KMS approach and the pseudonymization commitments for telemetry. Please go ahead and include the operational-custody-sla-draft.docx as DPA Annex A and send the DocuSign link for signatures. I'm looping contracts to expedite.

Emma Liu
Sr. Security PM, CardioHealth

Attachments referenced: CardioHealth_DPA_redline_20270928.pdf (redlines attached to our side)
